comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the gametogenesis characterization (C1-C3, C32-C33, C36) well-supported by live-cell imaging, DNA content analysis, and electron microscopy. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the bipartite MTOC structure characterization (C4, C5, C34). OpenEval notes C35 is not included in their evaluation, while peer review includes it. Both find the evidence convincing from expansion and electron microscopy.

Strong agreement on SUN1 conservation and localization (C6, C7, C37-C44). Peer review also includes spatial resolution claims (C45-C52) that OpenEval evaluates separately. Both find the fluorescence and electron microscopy data convincing.

Partial overlap. OpenEval evaluates spatial resolution data (C45-C50) separately as supported. Peer review groups these claims with broader SUN1 localization findings (R3) and accepts them as part of the comprehensive microscopy characterization.

Strong agreement on SUN1-ALLAN interaction (C8, C9, C79, C80). Both evaluations find the reciprocal immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry data convincing. OpenEval evaluates this separately from ALLAN localization, while peer review groups interaction and localization together.

Strong agreement on SUN1 knockout phenotype (C10, C12-C14, C53-C58, C62-C64). Both find the MTOC disruption, spindle defects, and transmission blockage well-documented. OpenEval includes ultrastructural details (C69-C74) here that peer review accepts within the same phenotypic characterization.

Agreement on ultrastructural defects in SUN1 knockout (C69-C74). OpenEval evaluates these separately as supported by U-ExM and TEM. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the overall SUN1 knockout phenotype characterization without separate discussion.

Agreement on genetic crossing experiments (C59-C61). OpenEval finds the male-specific requirement elegantly demonstrated. Peer review accepts these findings as part of the broader SUN1 functional characterization, with Reviewer 1 noting the convincing demonstration of male gamete requirement.

Perfect agreement on interactome data (C75-C78). Both evaluations find the immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry identification of protein associations convincing. Both note the bridging interpretation (C78) is inferential but reasonable.

Agreement on ALLAN localization (C81-C86). OpenEval finds the live-cell imaging and U-ExM data well-supported. Peer review groups ALLAN characterization with the SUN1-ALLAN complex identification and accepts the localization data as convincing.

Strong agreement on ALLAN knockout phenotype (C11, C87-C92). Both evaluations accept the differential severity compared to SUN1 knockout, with some transmission occurring despite most gametes being anucleate. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly notes the milder but still striking phenotype.

Perfect agreement on ALLAN ultrastructural defects (C93-C98). Both evaluations accept the basal body clustering, naked kinetochores, and the key observation that some normal gametes are produced, explaining the partial transmission phenotype.

Major disagreement on transcriptomic and lipidomic changes (C65-C68, C114). OpenEval finds the RNA-seq and lipidomic data supported with appropriate cautious interpretation. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly challenges these claims, stating statistical analysis is lacking and the data does not support claims about lipid composition changes. Editor agrees the lipid metabolism role is less well supported.

Agreement on phylogenetic analysis (C99-C103). Both evaluations accept the presence of two SUN proteins, two allantoicase subtypes, and absence of KASH/lamins. Peer Reviewer 1 notes the absence of KASH and suggests further work is needed to identify functional equivalents but does not challenge the findings.

Different evaluation levels. OpenEval rates AlphaFold3 modeling and evolutionary restriction (C104-C109) as UNCERTAIN due to moderate confidence scores and inferential nature. Peer reviewers accept the structural modeling and evolutionary analysis without critique, grouping it with the broader evolutionary findings.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C17-C18, C110-C113). Both evaluations find the essential nature of SUN1-ALLAN complex well-supported, the novelty established by absence of canonical LINC components, and the functional roles in MTOC coordination thoroughly documented. All reviewers call the work convincing and valuable.

OpenEval separately evaluates background/literature claims (C19-C31) as supported prior knowledge. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual claims, implicitly accepting them as appropriate background.

Agreement on female gametocyte SUN1 distribution (C51-C52). OpenEval evaluates this separately as supported with reasonable inference. Peer review includes these claims within the broader SUN1 localization characterization without separate discussion.

Partial disagreement. OpenEval finds lipid homeostasis claims (C114-C115) supported, though notes functional significance is unclear. Peer Reviewer 2 challenges the lipid composition claims (C114) as lacking statistical support. Both accept the evolutionary innovation characterization (C115) but peer review groups this with R10.
